sources.title: Pòta nèh: i segnali discorsivi del bergamasco contemporaneo (tesi magistrale)
sources.license: Thesis deposited in the University of Pavia repository (copyright of the author); consulted for facts and short attested examples
sources.reliability_notes: Read in full text locally (pdftotext). Orthography follows RID/Sanga. Gives sec. 5.4.1 on pòta/potà/'tà with attested spoken examples (16 speakers), glossary of discourse markers, summary of grammar (clitics, mìa, ö/ü, sibilant systems, -à-a imperfect). Speakers' Bergamasque mixes with Italian.
sources.author: Valentina Carrara
sources.publisher: Università degli Studi di Pavia, Dipartimento di Studi Umanistici

sources.title: Dialetto bergamasco (Wikipedia italiana)
sources.reliability_notes: Gives articles, obligatory subject clitics, full paradigms of èss, ìga, fà, regular verbs, demonstratives, plurals, negation mìa, ö/ü, aspirated h for s (sura > hura, sich > hich), history. Pronouns and some paradigms cross-checked against the Pavia thesis.
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors

sources.title: pota / potà / pòta (Wikizionario)
sources.reliability_notes: Lombard (Eastern) section: interjection with six listed uses and example scenes (written in Italian), pronunciation variants 'ta, 'òta, rarely Potà, lengthened Poòta, four dialect proverbs on the friar and on pòta, cites Zappettini 1859 p.389. No etymology given. Synonyms listed are vulgar. The Wikizionario spelling is Pòta.
sources.author: Wikizionario contributors

sources.title: Raccolta di proverbi bergamaschi (Wikisource, trascrizione)
sources.license: Public domain (Tiraboschi, 1875); Wikisource transcription CC BY-SA
sources.reliability_notes: Antonio Tiraboschi, Bergamo, Fratelli Bolis, 1875; proofreading incomplete (25-100% per chapter). Orthography is Tiraboschi's own 19th-century system (ć, ś, é/è, ö, ü) with Italian renderings. Chapters read: Famiglia, Fatti e parole, Contrattazioni, Allegria, Diligenza, Ira, Fortuna, Avvertimento.
sources.author: Antonio Tiraboschi
sources.relevant_sections: Famiglia; Fatti e parole; Contrattazioni; Allegria; Diligenza; Ira; Fortuna; Avvertimento

sources.title: Vocabolario bergamasco-italiano (Ducato di Piazza Pontida)
sources.license: Site content (cultural association); consulted for facts only
sources.reliability_notes: Online dictionary derived from Tiraboschi 1867 Vocabolario dei dialetti bergamaschi antichi e moderni and Caffi. Only the letter P page (pà to palèt) was readable; used for a few basic nouns. The landing page also states that the printed Francia-Gambarini dictionaries exist.
sources.author: Ducato di Piazza Pontida

sources.title: Italian profanity (Wikipedia)
sources.reliability_notes: Only one mention relevant here: the Bergamo dialect expression 'pota de Cristo' ('Christ's cunt') as an example of oaths that invoke the body of the Lord. No further Bergamasque items.
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors

sources.title: Bergamasque dialect (Wikipedia)
sources.reliability_notes: Classification (Gallo-Italic, Eastern Lombard), area (province of Bergamo, Crema), status (Regional Law 25/2016), sample texts showing ol, ö, ü. No grammar tables.
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors

sources.title: Lombard language (Wikipedia)
sources.reliability_notes: Only the first 100000 characters were read. Eastern Lombard debuccalization of the last sibilant to [h], ö/ü orthography, list of orthographies (Classical, Ticinese, Modern, Scriver, NOL). No Bergamasque grammar.
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors

sources.title: Dialèt bergamàsch (Wikipedia in lombardo)
sources.reliability_notes: Subject clitics are obligatory, mìa after the verb, orthography of the Ducato di Piazza Pontida is most used, vowel table. Little vocabulary. Confirms the clitic forms 'l, la, a m', i.
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors

sources.title: Impieghi simbolici (e non solo) del dialetto bergamasco nel paesaggio linguistico locale
sources.author: Federica Guerini
sources.reliability_notes: Read. Study of Bergamasque in shop signs, notices and banners; a pharmacy sign in dialect reads 'An sè dré a laùrà. An sè trasferès 50 meter piö n'ac. Pota, egnì a troàm!' (pota as an invitation, 'forza, venite a trovarci').
sources.publisher: Studi Italiani di Linguistica Teorica e Applicata
